sanskrit: na karmaṇā sādhunaikena nūnaṃ; kartuṃ śakyaṃ bhavatīha saṃjaya sarvātmanā parijetuṃ vayaṃ cen; na śaknumo dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putram
english: Surely by good deeds alone it cannot be done here, Sanjaya — to fully overcome them; for with all our might we are unable to defeat the son of Dhritarashtra.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yathārhase pāṇḍava tat tathaiva; kurūn kuruśreṣṭha janaṃ ca pṛcchasi anāmayās tāta manasvinas te; kuruśreṣṭhān pṛcchasi pārtha yāṃs tvam
english: Sanjaya said: As you deserve, O Pandava, even so it is; you ask after the Kurus, O best of Kurus, and after their people. May those wise ones of whom you ask, O Partha, be free from affliction, O dear one.

sanskrit: santy eva vṛddhāḥ sādhavo dhārtarāṣṭre; santy eva pāpāḥ pāṇḍava tasya viddhi dadyād ripoś cāpi hi dhārtarāṣṭraḥ; kuto dāyāṃl lopayed brāhmaṇānām
english: Among the Dhartarashtras there are indeed virtuous elders; there are also sinners among them — know this, O Pandava. The Dhartarashtra would give even to an enemy; how then would he withhold gifts from brahmins?

sanskrit: yad yuṣmākaṃ vartate 'sau na dharmyam; adrugdheṣu drugdhavat tan na sādhu mitradhruk syād dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputro; yuṣmān dviṣan sādhuvṛttān asādhuḥ
english: What he does toward you is not righteous; to act with hostility toward those who have not harmed him is not good. Dhritarashtra with his son has betrayed friends — he who is wicked despises you who are virtuous in conduct.

sanskrit: na cānujānāti bhṛśaṃ ca tapyate; śocaty antaḥ sthaviro 'jātaśatro śṛṇoti hi brāhmaṇānāṃ sametya; mitradrohaḥ pātakebhyo garīyān
english: He neither approves nor is he at peace, and he is deeply tormented; inwardly the old man grieves, O Ajatashatru. For he hears from assembled brahmins that treachery toward a friend is the gravest of all sins.

sanskrit: smaranti tubhyaṃ naradeva saṃgame; yuddhe ca jiṣṇoś ca yudhāṃ praṇetuḥ samutkṛṣṭe dundubhiśaṅkhaśabde; gadāpāṇiṃ bhīmasenaṃ smaranti
english: They remember you, O king of men, on the battlefield; and in war they remember Jishnu, the leader of warriors. When the roar of kettledrums and conches rises high, they remember Bhimasena with his mace in hand.

sanskrit: mādrīsutau cāpi raṇājimadhye; sarvā diśaḥ saṃpatantau smaranti senāṃ varṣantau śaravarṣair ajasraṃ; mahārathau samare duṣprakampyau
english: They also remember the two sons of Madri in the midst of the battle, ranging in all directions, incessantly showering arrows upon the army — two great warriors, impossible to shake in combat.

sanskrit: na tv eva manye puruṣasya rājann; anāgataṃ jñāyate yad bhaviṣyam tvaṃ ced imaṃ sarvadharmopapannaḥ; prāptaḥ kleśaṃ pāṇḍava kṛcchrarūpam
english: I do not think, O king, that the future of a man can be known in advance — what will come to pass. If you, O Pandava, endowed with all righteousness, have come to this severe and painful suffering —

sanskrit: tvam evaitat sarvam ataś ca bhūyaḥ; samīkuryāḥ prajñayājātaśatro na kāmārthaṃ saṃtyajeyur hi dharmaṃ; pāṇḍoḥ sutāḥ sarva evendrakalpāḥ
english: You alone should set all this right and even more, O Ajatashatru, through your wisdom. For the sons of Pandu, all equal to Indra, would never abandon dharma for the sake of desire or wealth.

sanskrit: tvam evaitat prajñayājātaśatro; śamaṃ kuryā yena śarmāpnuyus te dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś ca; ye cāpy anye pārthivāḥ saṃniviṣṭāḥ
english: You alone, O Ajatashatru, through your wisdom should bring about peace, whereby the Dhartarashtras, the Pandavas, and the Srinjayans, and whatever other kings are assembled, may all find happiness.

sanskrit: yan mābravīd dhṛtarāṣṭro niśāyām; ajātaśatro vacanaṃ pitā te sahāmātyaḥ sahaputraś ca rājan; sametya tāṃ vācam imāṃ nibodha
english: What Dhritarashtra, your father's brother, spoke to me at night, O Ajatashatru — together with his ministers and his sons, O king — hear now that speech of his.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca samāgatāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś ca; janārdano yuyudhāno virāṭaḥ yat te vākyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrānuśiṣṭaṃ; gāvalgaṇe brūhi tat sūtaputra
english: Yudhishthira said: The Pandavas and the Srinjayans are assembled, along with Janardana, Yuyudhana, and Virata. Speak, O son of Gavalgana, O son of a charioteer, that word instructed to you by Dhritarashtra.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ajātaśatruṃ ca vṛkodaraṃ ca; dhanaṃjayaṃ mādravatīsutau ca āmantraye vāsudevaṃ ca śauriṃ; yuyudhānaṃ cekitānaṃ virāṭam
english: Sanjaya said: I address Ajatashatru and Vrikodara, Dhananjaya and the two sons of Madravati, Vasudeva the Shauri, Yuyudhana, Chekitana, and Virata —

sanskrit: pāñcālānām adhipaṃ caiva vṛddhaṃ; dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ pārṣataṃ yājñasenim sarve vācaṃ śṛṇutemāṃ madīyāṃ; vakṣyāmi yāṃ bhūtim icchan kurūṇām
english: And the aged lord of the Panchalas, Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata, and the daughter of Yajnasena — let all of you hear this word of mine, which I shall speak desiring the welfare of the Kurus.

sanskrit: śamaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhinandann; ayojayat tvaramāṇo rathaṃ me sabhrātṛputrasvajanasya rājñas; tad rocatāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ śamo 'stu
english: King Dhritarashtra, welcoming peace, swiftly yoked my chariot on behalf of the king together with his brothers, sons, and kinsmen. Let this be pleasing — let there be peace for the Pandavas.

sanskrit: sarvair dharmaiḥ samupetāḥ stha pārthāḥ; prasthānena mārdavenārjavena jātāḥ kule anṛśaṃsā vadānyā; hrīniṣedhāḥ karmaṇāṃ niścayajñāḥ
english: You sons of Pritha are endowed with all virtues; by your lineage, your gentleness, and your straightforwardness, you are born into a noble family — compassionate, generous, restrained by modesty, and firm in resolve.

sanskrit: na yujyate karma yuṣmāsu hīnaṃ; sattvaṃ hi vas tādṛśaṃ bhīmasenāḥ udbhāsate hy añjanabinduvat tac; chukle vastre yad bhavet kilbiṣaṃ vaḥ
english: An ignoble act does not befit you, O Bhimasena; for your nature is such that even a blemish in you would stand out like a drop of collyrium on a white garment.

sanskrit: sarvakṣayo dṛśyate yatra kṛtsnaḥ; pāpodayo nirayo 'bhāvasaṃsthaḥ kas tat kuryāj jātu karma prajānan; parājayo yatra samo jayaś ca
english: Where total annihilation of all is seen, where sin arises and hell is ever present — who, knowing this, would ever commit that act where defeat is the same as victory?

sanskrit: te vai dhanyā yaiḥ kṛtaṃ jñātikāryaṃ; ye vaḥ putrāḥ suhṛdo bāndhavāś ca upakruṣṭaṃ jīvitaṃ saṃtyajeyus; tataḥ kurūṇāṃ niyato vai bhavaḥ syāt
english: Blessed indeed are those who have done their duty to kinsmen; your sons, friends, and relatives who would give up a life of reproach — from that would surely come the prosperity of the Kurus.

sanskrit: te cet kurūn anuśāsya stha pārthā; ninīya sarvān dviṣato nigṛhya samaṃ vas taj jīvitaṃ mṛtyunā syād; yaj jīvadhvaṃ jñātivadhe na sādhu
english: If you sons of Pritha were to govern the Kurus, leading all and subduing enemies, that life of yours would be equal to death — for to live by slaying kinsmen is not good.

sanskrit: ko hy eva yuṣmān saha keśavena; sacekitānān pārṣatabāhuguptān sasātyakīn viṣaheta prajetuṃ; labdhvāpi devān sacivān sahendrān
english: For who could endure to conquer you together with Keshava, protected by the arms of the son of Prishata, with Satyaki by your side — even having the gods as allies with Indra at their head?

sanskrit: ko vā kurūn droṇabhīṣmābhiguptān; aśvatthāmnā śalyakṛpādibhiś ca raṇe prasoḍhuṃ viṣaheta rājan; rādheyaguptān saha bhūmipālaiḥ
english: Or who could endure in battle to withstand the Kurus protected by Drona and Bhishma, and by Ashvatthama, Shalya, Kripa and others, O king — guarded by the son of Radha, together with the kings of earth?

sanskrit: mahad balaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya rājñaḥ; ko vai śakto hantum akṣīyamāṇaḥ so 'haṃ jaye caiva parājaye ca; niḥśreyasaṃ nādhigacchāmi kiṃ cit
english: The army of King Dhritarashtra's son is great; who indeed is capable of destroying it without himself being diminished? I myself see no lasting good in either victory or defeat.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi nīcā iva dauṣkuleyā; nirdharmārthaṃ karma kuryuś ca pārthāḥ so 'haṃ prasādya praṇato vāsudevaṃ; pāñcālānām adhipaṃ caiva vṛddham
english: For how could the sons of Pritha, like the baseborn from a low family, do deeds bereft of righteousness? I, having propitiated and bowed to Vasudeva and the aged lord of the Panchalas —

sanskrit: kṛtāñjaliḥ śaraṇaṃ vaḥ prapadye; kathaṃ svasti syāt kurusṛñjayānām na hy eva te vacanaṃ vāsudevo; dhanaṃjayo vā jātu kiṃ cin na kuryāt
english: With folded hands I take refuge with you all — how may there be welfare for the Kurus and the Srinjayans? For neither Vasudeva nor Dhananjaya would ever fail to act upon any word of yours.

sanskrit: prāṇān ādau yācyamānaḥ kuto 'nyad; etad vidvan sādhanārthaṃ bravīmi etad rājño bhīṣmapurogamasya; mataṃ yad vaḥ śāntir ihottamā syāt
english: When his very life is being asked first, what else remains? Knowing this, I speak for the sake of settlement. This is the view of the king, with Bhishma foremost among his counselors — that peace is the highest good for you here.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kāṃ nu vācaṃ saṃjaya me śṛṇoṣi; yuddhaiṣiṇīṃ yena yuddhād bibheṣi ayuddhaṃ vai tāta yuddhād garīyaḥ; kas tal labdhvā jātu yudhyeta sūta
english: Yudhishthira said: What word of mine do you hear, Sanjaya, as seeking war, that you fear battle? Non-war is indeed, dear one, greater than war; who, having obtained that, would ever fight, O charioteer?

sanskrit: akurvataś cet puruṣasya saṃjaya; sidhyet saṃkalpo manasā yaṃ yam icchet na karma kuryād viditaṃ mamaitad; anyatra yuddhād bahu yal laghīyaḥ
english: If, O Sanjaya, every intention a man wished for in his mind were to succeed without effort, then he would do no work — this is known to me. There is much that is far easier than war.

sanskrit: kuto yuddhaṃ jātu naraḥ prajānan; ko daivaśapto 'bhivṛṇīta yuddham sukhaiṣiṇaḥ karma kurvanti pārthā; dharmād ahīnaṃ yac ca lokasya pathyam
english: What man, truly knowing, would ever choose war? Who, unless cursed by fate, would embrace battle? The sons of Pritha act for the sake of happiness, and for what is not opposed to dharma and beneficial to the world.

sanskrit: karmodayaṃ sukham āśaṃsamānaḥ; kṛcchropāyaṃ tattvataḥ karma duḥkham sukhaprepsur vijighāṃsuś ca duḥkhaṃ; ya indriyāṇāṃ prītivaśānugāmī kāmābhidhyā svaśarīraṃ dunoti; yayā prayukto 'nukaroti duḥkham
english: One who, hoping for happiness arising from action, yet truly knows that action by arduous means is suffering — one who desires happiness and wishes to overcome suffering, yet follows the pull of the senses' pleasure, torments his own body through the craving of desire, and impelled by that craving, only brings suffering upon himself.

sanskrit: yathedhyamānasya samiddhatejaso; bhūyo balaṃ vardhate pāvakasya kāmārthalābhena tathaiva bhūyo; na tṛpyate sarpiṣevāgnir iddhaḥ saṃpaśyemaṃ bhogacayaṃ mahāntaṃ; sahāsmābhir dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rājñaḥ
english: Just as the power of fire blazing with its kindled splendor increases ever more, so too, with the gaining of wealth and desire, one is never satisfied — like a fire fed with ghee. Behold this vast accumulation of enjoyments belonging to King Dhritarashtra, together with us.

sanskrit: nāśreyasām īśvaro vigrahāṇāṃ; nāśreyasāṃ gītaśabdaṃ śṛṇoti nāśreyasaḥ sevate mālyagandhān; na cāpy aśreyāṃsy anulepanāni
english: The unrighteous man does not become a master of pleasures; the unrighteous man does not hear the sound of song; the unrighteous man does not enjoy garlands and perfumes, nor does the unrighteous one enjoy ointments.

sanskrit: nāśreyasaḥ prāvarān adhyavaste; kathaṃ tv asmān saṃpraṇudet kurubhyaḥ atraiva ca syād avadhūya eṣa; kāmaḥ śarīre hṛdayaṃ dunoti
english: The unrighteous man does not dwell in fine garments; then how could he drive us away from the Kurus? Right here, having shaken us off, this very desire torments the heart within the body.

sanskrit: svayaṃ rājā viṣamasthaḥ pareṣu; sāmasthyam anvicchati tan na sādhu yathātmanaḥ paśyati vṛttam eva; tathā pareṣām api so 'bhyupaiti
english: The king, himself in an uneven position, seeks evenness from others — that is not good. Just as one observes one's own conduct, so should one regard the conduct of others too.

sanskrit: āsannam agniṃ tu nidāghakāle; gambhīrakakṣe gahane visṛjya yathā vṛddhaṃ vāyuvaśena śocet; kṣemaṃ mumukṣuḥ śiśiravyapāye
english: Just as one who, having set a fire near deep, dense thickets of dry grass in the hot season, would grieve as the old fire spreads under the wind — so too the one seeking safety laments when winter passes.

sanskrit: prāptaiśvaryo dhṛtarāṣṭro 'dya rājā; lālapyate saṃjaya kasya hetoḥ pragṛhya durbuddhim anārjave rataṃ; putraṃ mandaṃ mūḍham amantriṇam tu
english: Having attained sovereignty, King Dhritarashtra now laments — for what reason, O Sanjaya? He clings to a son of wicked intellect, devoted to crookedness, dull, foolish, and without counsel.

sanskrit: anāptaḥ sann āptatamasya vācaṃ; suyodhano vidurasyāvamanya sutasya rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ priyaiṣī; saṃbudhyamāno viśate 'dharmam eva
english: Though unworthy, Suyodhana disregarded the words of the most trustworthy Vidura; and King Dhritarashtra, doting on his son, though perceiving rightly, yet enters into unrighteousness.

sanskrit: medhāvinaṃ hy arthakāmaṃ kurūṇāṃ; bahuśrutaṃ vāgminaṃ śīlavantam sūta rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ kurubhyo; na so 'smarad viduraṃ putrakāmyāt
english: The intelligent one, devoted to the welfare of the Kurus, the learned, eloquent, and virtuous Vidura — King Dhritarashtra, O charioteer, forgot him in the affairs of the Kurus out of love for his son.

sanskrit: mānaghnasya ātmakāmasya cerṣyoḥ; saṃrambhiṇaś cārthadharmātigasya durbhāṣiṇo manyuvaśānugasya; kāmātmano durhṛdo bhāvanasya
english: Of one who destroys honor, who is self-seeking and envious, violent and transgressing wealth and dharma, foul-spoken, enslaved to anger, whose soul is given over to desire, whose heart is wicked, and who is always calculating —

sanskrit: aneyasyāśreyaso dīrghamanyor; mitradruhaḥ saṃjaya pāpabuddheḥ sutasya rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ priyaiṣī; prapaśyamānaḥ prajahād dharmakāmau
english: Of such a son — ungovernable, inauspicious, long-resentful, a betrayer of friends, O Sanjaya, of sinful mind — King Dhritarashtra, though clearly seeing, abandoned dharma and righteous desire out of love.

sanskrit: tadaiva me saṃjaya dīvyato 'bhūn; no cet kurūn āgataḥ syād abhāvaḥ kāvyāṃ vācaṃ viduro bhāṣamāṇo; na vindate dhṛtarāṣṭrāt praśaṃsām
english: Even then, O Sanjaya, it was evident to me when I was in prosperity: unless the Kurus met with ruin. Vidura, speaking words of wisdom, found no appreciation from Dhritarashtra.

sanskrit: kṣattur yadā anvavartanta buddhiṃ; kṛcchraṃ kurūn na tadābhyājagāma yāvat prajñām anvavartanta tasya; tāvat teṣāṃ rāṣṭravṛddhir babhūva
english: When they followed the counsel of Vidura, hardship did not come upon the Kurus; so long as they followed his wisdom, so long did the prosperity of their kingdom flourish.

sanskrit: tadarthalubdhasya nibodha me 'dya; ye mantriṇo dhārtarāṣṭrasya sūta duḥśāsanaḥ śakuniḥ sūtaputro; gāvalgaṇe paśya saṃmoham asya
english: Know from me today, O son of Gavalgana, the counselors of the greedy Dhartarashtra — Duhshasana, Shakuni, and the son of a charioteer — behold his delusion!

sanskrit: so 'haṃ na paśyāmi parīkṣamāṇaḥ; kathaṃ svasti syāt kurusṛñjayānām āttaiśvaryo dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ parebhyaḥ; pravrājite vidure dīrghadṛṣṭau
english: I, examining carefully, cannot see how there may be welfare for the Kurus and the Srinjayans, when Dhritarashtra has taken sovereignty over others and banished Vidura of far-seeing wisdom.

sanskrit: āśaṃsate vai dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputro; mahārājyam asapatnaṃ pṛthivyām tasmiñ śamaḥ kevalaṃ nopalabhyo; atyāsannaṃ madgataṃ manyate 'rtham
english: Indeed Dhritarashtra and his son hope for undisputed sovereignty over the entire earth; from him no trace of peace is to be found. He thinks the matter that belongs to me is already close at hand and in his grasp.

sanskrit: yat tat karṇo manyate pāraṇīyaṃ; yuddhe gṛhītāyudham arjunena āsaṃś ca yuddhāni purā mahānti; kathaṃ karṇo nābhavad dvīpa eṣām
english: What Karna thinks he can sustain in battle, when Arjuna has taken up his weapon — great battles were fought in the past; why was Karna not their refuge even then?

sanskrit: karṇaś ca jānāti suyodhanaś ca; droṇaś ca jānāti pitāmahaś ca anye ca ye kuravas tatra santi; yathārjunān nāsty aparo dhanurdharaḥ
english: Karna knows, and Suyodhana knows, Drona knows, and the grandfather knows, and the other Kurus who are there — that there is no other bowman equal to Arjuna.

sanskrit: jānanty ete kuravaḥ sarva eva; ye cāpy anye bhūmipālāḥ sametāḥ duryodhanaṃ cāparādhe carantam; ariṃdame phalgune 'vidyamāne
english: All these Kurus know, and so do the other kings assembled there, that Duryodhana has been acting in transgression, and that without Phalguna the subduer of foes, there would be none.

sanskrit: tenārthabaddhaṃ manyate dhārtarāṣṭraḥ; śakyaṃ hartuṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mamatvam kirīṭinā tālamātrāyudhena; tadvedinā saṃyugaṃ tatra gatvā
english: The son of Dhritarashtra thinks that by reason of his wealth it is possible to seize the possessions of the Pandavas — with the diademed one, whose weapon is as tall as a palm tree, going to the battlefield and knowing that ground.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvavisphāritaśabdam ājāv; aśṛṇvānā dhārtarāṣṭrā dhriyante kruddhasya ced bhīmasenasya vegāt; suyodhano manyate siddham artham
english: The Dhartarashtras survive only because they have not yet heard the twang of the Gandiva in battle; and if the onset of the enraged Bhimasena has not come — Suyodhana thinks his purpose already accomplished.

sanskrit: indro 'py etan notsahet tāta hartum; aiśvaryaṃ no jīvati bhīmasene dhanaṃjaye nakule caiva sūta; tathā vīre sahadeve madīye
english: Even Indra would not dare to seize this sovereignty of ours, dear one, as long as Bhimasena lives, as long as Dhananjaya, Nakula, O charioteer, and likewise that hero Sahadeva of mine live.

sanskrit: sa ced etāṃ pratipadyeta buddhiṃ; vṛddho rājā saha putreṇa sūta evaṃ raṇe pāṇḍavakopadagdhā; na naśyeyuḥ saṃjaya dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
english: If the aged king together with his son were to adopt this resolve, O charioteer — then the Dhartarashtras would not perish, O Sanjaya, burned by the wrath of the Pandavas in battle.

sanskrit: jānāsi tvaṃ kleśam asmāsu vṛttaṃ; tvāṃ pūjayan saṃjayāhaṃ kṣameyam yac cāsmākaṃ kauravair bhūtapūrvaṃ; yā no vṛttir dhārtarāṣṭre tadāsīt
english: You know the suffering that has been inflicted upon us; honoring you, O Sanjaya, I would endure it. And what the Kauravas did to us in the past — the treatment we received from the son of Dhritarashtra — that too I could bear.

sanskrit: adyāpi tat tatra tathaiva vartatāṃ; śāntiṃ gamiṣyāmi yathā tvam āttha indraprasthe bhavatu mamaiva rājyaṃ; suyodhano yacchatu bhāratāgryaḥ
english: Even now let all that continue as it is there; I shall pursue peace as you say. Let Indraprastha be my kingdom alone — let Suyodhana, foremost of the Bharatas, grant that much.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dharme nityā pāṇḍava te viceṣṭā; loke śrutā dṛśyate cāpi pārtha mahāsrāvaṃ jīvitaṃ cāpy anityaṃ; saṃpaśya tvaṃ pāṇḍava mā vinīnaśaḥ
english: Sanjaya said: Your conduct, O Pandava, is ever fixed in dharma; it is heard of and seen in the world, O Partha. Life is a great torrent and also impermanent — perceive this, O Pandava; do not bring yourself to ruin.

sanskrit: na ced bhāgaṃ kuravo 'nyatra yuddhāt; prayacchante tubhyam ajātaśatro bhaikṣacaryām andhakavṛṣṇirājye; śreyo manye na tu yuddhena rājyam
english: If the Kurus do not grant you a share except through war, O Ajatashatru, I think it better to live by begging in the kingdom of the Andhakas and Vrishnis than to rule through war.

sanskrit: alpakālaṃ jīvitaṃ yan manuṣye; mahāsrāvaṃ nityaduḥkhaṃ calaṃ ca bhūyaś ca tad vayaso nānurūpaṃ; tasmāt pāpaṃ pāṇḍava mā prasārṣīḥ
english: Life in the human world is brief, a great torrent, constantly painful, and unstable; and it is further unworthy of the dignity of your age. Therefore, O Pandava, do not set evil in motion.

sanskrit: kāmā manuṣyaṃ prasajanta eva; dharmasya ye vighnamūlaṃ narendra pūrvaṃ naras tān dhṛtimān vinighnaṃl; loke praśaṃsāṃ labhate 'navadyām
english: Desires indeed bind a man — they are the very root of obstruction to dharma, O king of men. A man of firm resolve who first crushes them wins blameless praise in the world.

sanskrit: nibandhanī hy arthatṛṣṇeha pārtha; tām eṣato bādhyate dharma eva dharmaṃ tu yaḥ pravṛṇīte sa buddhaḥ; kāme gṛddho hīyate 'rthānurodhāt
english: The craving for wealth is the binding fetter here, O Partha; dharma itself is obstructed when one pursues that craving. But the one who chooses dharma is wise; the one greedy for pleasure falls away, following the pull of wealth.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ kṛtvā karmaṇāṃ tāta mukhyaṃ; mahāpratāpaḥ saviteva bhāti hānena dharmasya mahīm apīmāṃ; labdhvā naraḥ sīdati pāpabuddhiḥ
english: Having made dharma the foremost of all actions, dear one, the man of great splendor shines like the sun; but through the abandonment of dharma, a man of sinful mind sinks even having gained this entire earth.

sanskrit: vedo 'dhītaś caritaṃ brahmacaryaṃ; yajñair iṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaś ca dattam paraṃ sthānaṃ manyamānena bhūya; ātmā datto varṣapūgaṃ sukhebhyaḥ
english: The Vedas studied, the vow of brahmacharya observed, sacrifices performed, gifts given to brahmins — one who considers the highest state supreme and again gives up the self from pleasures for many years —

sanskrit: sukhapriye sevamāno 'tivelaṃ; yogābhyāse yo na karoti karma vittakṣaye hīnasukho 'tivelaṃ; duḥkhaṃ śete kāmavegapraṇunnaḥ
english: One who excessively indulges in pleasure and what is dear, and does not practice the discipline of yoga — when his wealth is exhausted, diminished in happiness, he lies in endless suffering, driven by the impulse of desire.

sanskrit: evaṃ punar arthacaryāprasakto; hitvā dharmaṃ yaḥ prakaroty adharmam aśraddadhat paralokāya mūḍho; hitvā dehaṃ tapyate pretya mandaḥ
english: Thus, once more attached to the pursuit of wealth, one who abandons dharma and propagates unrighteousness — the foolish one, lacking faith in the next world, after leaving the body suffers in the realm of the dead, the dull one.

sanskrit: na karmaṇāṃ vipraṇāśo 'sty amutra; puṇyānāṃ vāpy atha vā pāpakānām pūrvaṃ kartur gacchati puṇyapāpaṃ; paścāt tv etad anuyāty eva kartā
english: There is no destruction of deeds in the hereafter, whether of merit or of sin. The merit and sin of the doer go ahead of him; afterward the doer himself follows them.

sanskrit: nyāyopetaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo yadannaṃ; śraddhāpūtaṃ gandharasopapannam anvāhāryeṣūttamadakṣiṇeṣu; tathārūpaṃ karma vikhyāyate te
english: Food offered to brahmins in the proper manner, purified by faith, endowed with fragrance and flavor, at funerary rites with the finest fees — such deeds as these are celebrated to your credit.

sanskrit: iha kṣetre kriyate pārtha kāryaṃ; na vai kiṃ cid vidyate pretya kāryam kṛtaṃ tvayā pāralokyaṃ ca kāryaṃ; puṇyaṃ mahat sadbhir anupraśastam
english: Here in this field, O Partha, is the action to be done; truly nothing remains to be done after death. What you have done — and the duty for the next world — is great merit praised by the righteous.

sanskrit: jahāti mṛtyuṃ ca jarāṃ bhayaṃ ca; na kṣutpipāse manasaś cāpriyāṇi na kartavyaṃ vidyate tatra kiṃ cid; anyatra vai indriyaprīṇanārthāt
english: He abandons death, old age, and fear, hunger and thirst, and the unpleasantnesses of the mind — nothing remains to be done there, except for the satisfaction of the senses.

sanskrit: evaṃrūpaṃ karmaphalaṃ narendra; mātrāvatā hṛdayasya priyeṇa sa krodhajaṃ pāṇḍava harṣajaṃ ca; lokāv ubhau mā prahāsīś cirāya
english: Such is the fruit of action, O king of men; with what is dear to the heart in its proper measure — do not, O Pandava, give up both worlds for a long time for the sake of what is born of anger or of joy.

sanskrit: antaṃ gatvā karmaṇāṃ yā praśaṃsā; satyaṃ damaś cārjavam ānṛśaṃsyam aśvamedho rājasūyas tatheṣṭaḥ; pāpasyāntaṃ karmaṇo mā punar gāḥ
english: The praise that comes at the end of righteous deeds — truth, restraint, straightforwardness, compassion; the ashvamedha and the rajasuya duly performed — do not again go toward the end of sinful deeds.

sanskrit: tac ced evaṃ deśarūpeṇa pārthāḥ; kariṣyadhvaṃ karma pāpaṃ cirāya nivasadhvaṃ varṣapūgān vaneṣu; duḥkhaṃ vāsaṃ pāṇḍavā dharmahetoḥ
english: If you sons of Pritha are to commit this sinful act for a long time in the manner it seems, then dwell for years in the forests, O Pandavas — a painful dwelling for the sake of dharma.

sanskrit: apravrajye yojayitvā purastād; ātmādhīnaṃ yad balaṃ te tadāsīt nityaṃ pāñcālāḥ sacivās taveme; janārdano yuyudhānaś ca vīraḥ
english: Before going into exile, having arrayed the force that was then under your own command — always the Panchalas as your allies, Janardana and the heroic Yuyudhana —

sanskrit: matsyo rājā rukmarathaḥ saputraḥ; prahāribhiḥ saha putrair virāṭaḥ rājānaś ca ye vijitāḥ purastāt; tvām eva te saṃśrayeyuḥ samastāḥ
english: Matsya the king of the golden chariot with his sons, Virata with his warrior sons, and the kings who were previously conquered by you — all of them would take refuge in you.

sanskrit: mahāsahāyaḥ pratapan balasthaḥ; puraskṛto vāsudevārjunābhyām varān haniṣyan dviṣato raṅgamadhye; vyaneṣyathā dhārtarāṣṭrasya darpam
english: With great allies, blazing with power, standing in strength, placed at the fore by Vasudeva and Arjuna, you would have struck down the best of your enemies in the midst of the arena and crushed the pride of the Dhartarashtra.

sanskrit: balaṃ kasmād vardhayitvā parasya; nijān kasmāt karśayitvā sahāyān niruṣya kasmād varṣapūgān vaneṣu; yuyutsase pāṇḍava hīnakālam
english: Why did you strengthen the power of the enemy? Why did you exhaust your own allies? Why did you spend years dwelling in the forests? Now, O Pandava, you wish to fight at an unfavorable time.

sanskrit: aprajño vā pāṇḍava yudhyamāno; adharmajño vā bhūtipathād vyapaiti prajñāvān vā budhyamāno 'pi dharmaṃ; saṃrambhād vā so 'pi bhūter apaiti
english: Either the unwise man fighting, O Pandava, or the one ignorant of adharma, strays from the path of prosperity; or even the wise man, though perceiving dharma, may through anger also stray from prosperity.

sanskrit: nādharme te dhīyate pārtha buddhir; na saṃrambhāt karma cakartha pāpam addhā kiṃ tat kāraṇaṃ yasya hetoḥ; prajñāviruddhaṃ karma cikīrṣasīdam
english: Your mind, O Partha, does not dwell on unrighteousness; and you have not committed sinful deeds out of anger. What then is that reason for whose sake you wish to commit this act that goes against wisdom?

sanskrit: avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ śīrṣarogaṃ; yaśomuṣaṃ pāpaphalodayaṃ ca satāṃ peyaṃ yan na pibanty asanto; manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya
english: Anger — not born of disease, yet bitter as a headache, a thief of glory, productive of sinful fruits — which the righteous drink but the wicked do not drink — drink it, O great king, and be at peace.

sanskrit: pāpānubandhaṃ ko nu taṃ kāmayeta; kṣamaiva te jyāyasī nota bhogāḥ yatra bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo hataḥ syād; yatra droṇaḥ sahaputro hataḥ syāt
english: Who would desire that which is followed by sin? Forgiveness is indeed greater for you than enjoyments. Where Bhishma the son of Shantanu would be slain, where Drona with his son would be slain —

sanskrit: kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ saumadattir vikarṇo; viviṃśatiḥ karṇaduryodhanau ca etān hatvā kīdṛśaṃ tat sukhaṃ syād; yad vindethās tad anubrūhi pārtha
english: Kripa, Shalya, the son of Somadatta, Vikarna, Vivinshatí, Karna and Duryodhana — having slain these, what sort of happiness could there be? Tell me what joy you would find, O Partha.

sanskrit: labdhvāpīmāṃ pṛthivīṃ sāgarāntāṃ; jarāmṛtyū naiva hi tvaṃ prajahyāḥ priyāpriye sukhaduḥkhe ca rājann; evaṃ vidvān naiva yuddhaṃ kuruṣva
english: Even having gained this entire earth bounded by the ocean, you would not escape old age and death, O king, nor the pleasant and the unpleasant, pleasure and pain. Knowing this, do not make war.
